topic.readerProblem: Test brand-mention entity resolution without merging products, parents, subsidiaries, namesakes, or ambiguous aliases.
topic.connection: Brand identity matching determines the numerator for AI visibility, recommendation, and citation metrics produced by AEO audits.

assessment: The page provides a runnable twenty-four-case synthetic corpus and narrow reference matcher. It exercises exact, normalized, ambiguous, and no-match branches while preserving separate entity IDs for products, parents, subsidiaries, and namesakes instead of maximizing match rate.

sources.supports: Unicode normalization forms and the warning that compatibility normalization can remove distinctions.
The Unicode database and normalization function used by the matcher.
The organization vocabulary discussed as one possible identity evidence source rather than proof.
The provenance concepts used to retain raw observed strings and later matching decisions.

checks: Ran all twenty-four cases to a separate actual.csv and confirmed a byte-for-byte match with the immutable expected.csv fixture.
Corrected the original self-comparison workflow and added four cases that genuinely execute the NFKC, case-fold, and separator-normalization branch.
Read every fixture row and final section, verified ambiguous aliases remain review, checked parent and product IDs stay separate, and corrected the second image's author and literal alt text.

artifacts.description: Populated synthetic entity registry with canonical, domain, short-name, legal-name, and collision aliases.
Twenty-four populated synthetic observations spanning exact, normalized, ambiguous, compound, and undeclared names.
Dependency-free exact-first matcher with a unique normalized-alias fallback and explicit review state.
Deterministic checked output used for a true separate-file byte comparison.
Run contract, synthetic-data warning, and guidance for evidence-backed extensions.

methodology: The review generated a separate output file, compared it byte-for-byte, inspected all twenty-four observed names and entity IDs, forced actual normalized-branch coverage with full-width, case, spacing, and punctuation variants, and confirmed ambiguous exact and normalized keys never receive a guessed entity.
limitations: The corpus is not a real entity benchmark. It cannot infer legal identity, ownership, redirects, multilingual equivalence, answer context, provider tokenization, or whether a mention is a recommendation.
